title: Starter runtime telemetry playbook for SDK ambassadors (draft)
content:
Purpose: Provide a compact, pragmatic telemetry onboarding and runbook targeted at SDK ambassadors (internal engineers who ship SDK examples, demos, and customer onboarding flows). This is intentionally lightweight: tags, event names, sampling heuristics, and a short checklist so ambassadors can instrument quickly and avoid noisy or PII-leaking events.

Audience: SDK integrators, developer advocates, solutions engineers, and on-call engineers who maintain the example apps we hand to customers. Not intended as the full observability spec for runtime teams.

Goals / success metrics (what ambassadors care about):
- Time to useful insight: median time from adding instrumentation to seeing a dashboard card = < 48h.
- Telemetry cost guardrail: incremental ingestion from sample apps < 5% of team budget.
- Actionable alerts: < 3 false positives per week on runbook-generated alerts.
- Privacy safe: zero PII events stored in raw telemetry.

High-level principles (decisions to keep small):
- Minimal event surface: prefer a few well-scoped events with contextual tags rather than many tiny events.
- Defaults must be conservative: low sampling by default, clear opt-in for verbose traces.
- Remove vs. redact: redact sensitive strings before emitting; avoid storing raw user input.
- Short retention for dev/demo apps: 7–30 days unless explicitly promoted.

Minimal event set (recommended) — aim to instrument these 6 events:
1) sdk.startup (when SDK client is constructed) — tags: sdk_version, runtime, env (demo|prod|sandbox), oauth_present (y/n)
2) api.request (single record per request routed to Redwood) — tags: model, route, seq_len_estimate, cache_hit (y/n), batching_enabled (y/n), latency_ms_bucket
3) api.response.summary (high level success/failure, tokens_out, tokens_in, cost_estimate_usd) — no raw text
4) kvcache.hit (incremental) — tags: key_len_bucket, hit_latency_ms
5) fallback.triggered (when ambassador flow uses fallback model or cached stub) — tags: reason_code, fallback_model
6) sdk.error (surface errors with numeric code and sparse context) — must never include stack traces with user input

Event format notes: All events should follow our short JSON envelope: {"event":"<name>","ts":"<iso>","tags":"…"}. Keep payload small. Avoid embedding whole requests or responses.

Sampling and retention guidance:
- Default sample rate for api.request in demo/sandbox envs = 2%. Increase to 10% for short troubleshooting windows (max 48h).
- For production customer SDKs (if instrumented), default sample = 0.2% unless the customer explicitly opts in via managed telemetry setting.
- Full traces (span-level) are disabled by default. Use a trace flag gated behind feature flag and auditing.
- Retention: demo/sandbox data = 7 days; ambassador promoted staging apps = 30 days.

Privacy & PII guardrails (non-negotiable):
- Never send raw user prompts, documents, or embeddings to telemetry. Always send redacted summaries or hashes.
- If an event needs to reference a prompt, send prompt_length_bucket and a sha256 prompt_hash (no salt).
- Personal identifiers (email, phone, SSN) must be redacted server-side before event emission. If unsure, redact.
- Ambassadors: provide a pre-commit linter rule that blocks sending event fields named "user_text", "prompt", "document".

Dashboarding and recommended cards (starter set):
- SDK Health Summary: api.request qps, median latency, error rate (5xx, 4xx), cache hit rate.
- Econometrics: avg tokens_in/out per request, estimated cost per 1000 reqs, trend line.
- Failure triage: top 5 error codes over last 24h with sample IDs.
- Ambassadors' quickprobe: sampling rate, events emitted per minute, ingestion size last 24h.
- Regression watch: baseline metrics vs last deploy (latency delta, cost delta).

Alerting suggestions (low-noise defaults):
- P1: error rate spike: if 5xx rate > 2% for 10m AND absolute errors > 5 in 10m => page SRE oncall.
- P2: latency tail erosion: p99 latency increases by > 35% vs baseline for 15m => slack alert #devexp-telemetry.
- P3: telemetry budget threshold: if ingestion projected to exceed 80% of monthly demo budget => email to ambassador and devexp lead.

Ambassador onboarding checklist (10–15 min run):
- [ ] Pull example app branch "telemetry-ambassador-starter"
- [ ] Add sdk.startup and api.request events following template (see Appendix)
- [ ] Ensure no prompt text is emitted; run local pre-commit linter to validate
- [ ] Deploy to demo env with sample_rate set to 2%
- [ ] Open SDK Health Summary dashboard and verify events show up (within ~30–60m)
- [ ] Run 5 synthetic flows to verify fallback.triggered and kvcache.hit cards populate
- [ ] Document required JIRA if increasing retention or adding new event types

Quickstart snippet (pseudo-code, fill in SDK specific APIs):
# python-like snippet
# emit minimal event without user text
client = RedwoodSDKClient(api_key=ENV_VAR)
emit_event("sdk.startup", tags={"sdk_version":"0.9.3","runtime":"python","env":"demo"})
resp = client.generate(prompt_stub_hash="<hash>")
emit_event("api.request", tags={"model":"gptx-8b","seq_len_estimate":"short","cache_hit":"n"})
# on response summary
emit_event("api.response.summary", tags={"success":"y","tokens_out":"32","tokens_in":"10"})

Notes to self (working/fragile):
- We need a small JS/TS wrapper that enforces redaction rules for browser SDKs; current browser SDKs sometimes capture text accidentally via auto-fill.
- Confirm whether customer-managed telemetry option changes sampling semantics (ask infra/legal).
- Costs: identify which demo apps are on shared ingestion bucket vs per-team. Reduce retention or increase sampling accordingly.

Unresolved questions / decisions for RFC:
- Should prompt_hash be salted? Pros: prevents rainbow tables; cons: breaks dedupable cross-app analysis. Proposed: no salt for demo apps, salt optional for customer-managed telemetry with explicit opt-in.
- Do we expose cost_estimate_usd at event-level? Quick wins for dashboards but may leak pricing decisions. Proposed: keep cost_estimate_usd in aggregated pipelines only.

Next steps & owners:
- Build pre-commit linter rule and include in starter repo (owner: Marcus) — ETA 2025-12-05.
- Prototype JS redaction wrapper and test in browser sample app (owner: Lina) — ETA 2026-01-10.
- Create baseline dashboard templates and import into demo org (owner: Owen) — ETA 2026-01-20.
- Follow-up RFC for prompt_hash salting and long-term retention (owner: Aisha) — ETA 2026-02-01.

Appendix: example minimal event lines (what to expect in logs)
- 2026-01-15T14:02:31Z | event=sdk.startup | tags=sdk_version:0.9.3,runtime:node,env:demo
- 2026-01-15T14:02:37Z | event=api.request | tags=model:gptx-8b,seq_len_estimate:short,cache_hit:n,latency_ms_bucket:50-100
- 2026-01-15T14:02:37Z | event=api.response.summary | tags=success:y,tokens_in:12,tokens_out:48,cost_estimate_usd:0.0012

Quick links / references:
- Telemetry primer (Confluence): CONFLUENCE-RT-1234
- Starter repo branch: github.com/redwood-inference/sdks/tree/telemetry-ambassador-starter
- Slack channel: #devexp-telemetry (linked_artifacts above)

If you're the ambassador reading this: try the 10–15 minute onboarding checklist, file a short retrospective (2 bullets) into the repo's /telemetry/retrospectives.md. If anything trips you up, tag @Aisha in #devexp-telemetry and we will fix the template within 48h.

-- end of draft (feel free to break into separate doc for RFC items).
